contract.name: StreamingPayments
contract.description: Continuous, linear streaming payments on Stellar (Soroban).

functions.name: create_stream
functions.doc:
Creates a linear payment stream and pulls `deposit_amount` of `token`
from `sender` into this contract.

The sender must first approve this contract as a spender on `token`
(`token.approve(sender, streaming_contract, deposit_amount, ...)`).
When a protocol fee is configured, the approval (and the pull) cover
`deposit_amount + fee`, where `fee = deposit_amount * fee_bps / 10_000`
is charged once, here at the deposit boundary — never during
accrual or payout. At `fee_bps == 0` the call is identical to the
fee-less contract: same pull, same events, same state.

* `start_time` must not be in the past (UIs pass the current time to
  start streaming immediately).
* `end_time` must be strictly after `start_time` (zero-duration streams
  are rejected) and at most `MAX_DURATION_SECONDS` long.
* `cancelable` controls whether the recipient may also call
  `cancel_stream` to reclaim their accrued balance.

Returns the new stream id (monotonically increasing, starting at 1).

The deposit pull is mapped to [`StreamError::DepositTransferFailed`]
(missing balance/allowance, or an asset that refuses the transfer);
nothing is persisted when it fails, so no stream id is consumed.

functions.name: create_stream_with_oracle
functions.doc: Creates a payment stream with optional oracle reference time source.

functions.name: create_stream_with_refund
functions.doc:
Creates a stream whose unstreamed remainder is refundable to `refund_to`
rather than to the sender.

The refund claim normally travels with the sender role; pinning it at
creation is how a payer routes a cancellation back to the account that
actually funded the deposit — a treasury behind the signing key, a
corporate payer whose payroll wallet is ephemeral, or a parent grant that
must reclaim what its beneficiary's stream never spent. Accrual, the
recipient's claims and `cancel_stream`'s authorization are untouched: only
the destination of the *remainder* changes, so
`0 <= withdrawn <= streamed <= deposit` and the conservation invariant are
identical to [`StreamingPayments::create_stream`].

`refund_to` must differ from `sender` — that is already where the claim
sits, and refusing the no-op keeps the event log to real routing changes.
The address is *not* required to exist, hold a balance, or be able to
receive: routing to an address that cannot accept the transfer surfaces
later as [`StreamError::SenderRefundFailed`] on the cancellation, so this
is the sender's own risk to take, and the reason the choice is announced
by `StreamRefundTargetChanged` rather than stored silently.

functions.name: set_refund_target
functions.doc:
Re-routes the refund of a stream's unstreamed remainder to `refund_to`.

Only the current sender may call this, and only while the stream is
`Active`: the claim is the counterpart of the money that funded the
stream, so nobody else gets to redirect it, and once the stream is
cancelled or depleted there is no remainder left to route.

Routing to the sender's own address is the way to *undo* a previous
routing (or to make a routed claim follow the role again), and is a real
change whenever the pinned target differs from the current sender — see
[`StreamingPayments::refund_target`].

The claim is deliberately *not* re-derived from the role on every hop: a
consented sender transfer keeps whatever routing was in force, which is
why [`StreamingPayments::propose_sender_transfer`] carries an explicit
`transfer_refund_rights` flag instead of implying one here. A top-up by a
later sender therefore enlarges the pot that the *pinned* target reclaims
— route with intent.

functions.name: create_streams
functions.doc:
Creates multiple streams atomically, authorizing the sender once and
grouping deposits into one token pull per token. Every item uses the
same validation and fee rules as `create_stream`; if any item is
invalid, the entire transaction (including transfers and state writes)
is rolled back. An empty input returns an empty vector without auth.

Emits one `StreamsCreated` event containing all ids; individual
`FeeCharged` events are still emitted when fees apply.

functions.name: create_streams_batch
functions.doc:
Creates a batch of payment streams in a single transaction.

Semantics are all-or-nothing per entry but best-effort across the batch:
each entry validates its parameters and attempts its own deposit pull.
Failures are reported per-entry in the returned vector without aborting
or rolling back successfully created sibling streams.

The entire batch call reverts if `entries` is empty ([`StreamError::BatchEmpty`])
or exceeds [`MAX_BATCH`] ([`StreamError::BatchTooLarge`]).

functions.name: withdraw
functions.doc:
Withdraws up to `amount` of the accrued-but-unwithdrawn balance and
pays it to the stream recipient. Only the recipient can call this
(their authorization is required).

Reverts with [`StreamError::AmountExceedsAvailable`] if `amount`
exceeds what has accrued so far; before `start_time` nothing has
accrued, at or after `end_time` the full remainder is available.

A token-side failure to deliver the payout returns
[`StreamError::RecipientPayoutFailed`] and rolls the recorded
`withdrawn` update back with it.

# Ordering against `cancel_stream` (same-ledger race)

`withdraw` and `cancel_stream` are strictly serial: each invocation
runs to completion — including its CEI state writes — before the next
begins, even when both land in the same ledger. There is no
interleaving and no partial application; whichever call executes
first wins, and the loser observes the post-write state:

* If `cancel_stream` executes first, the stream is already `Cancelled`
  when `withdraw` runs, so it reverts with
  [`StreamError::StreamNotActive`] (code 5) without moving tokens.
* If `withdraw` executes first, a subsequent `cancel_stream` splits
  only the *remaining* balance (`streamed − withdrawn`). If this
  withdrawal drained the stream (`withdrawn == deposit`, status
  `Depleted`), the cancel instead reverts with
  [`StreamError::StreamNotActive`] (code 5).

The losing call never mutates state, so the funds-conservation
outcome is identical to the serial composition: the recipient
receives exactly the amount accrued at the later call and the sender
is refunded the unaccrued remainder. Regression tests pin these
sequences in `test.rs` (`race_*`); the race table lives in
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §6.1.

functions.name: withdraw_max
functions.doc:
Withdraws the entire accrued-but-unwithdrawn balance in one call and
returns the amount paid. Only the recipient can call this (their
authorization is required).

This is the atomic form of "read `available`, then `withdraw` it":
clients never risk a stale amount between the two calls. Reverts with
[`StreamError::NothingToWithdraw`] when nothing has accrued yet (or
everything accrued has already been withdrawn), with
[`StreamError::StreamNotActive`] on cancelled or depleted streams, and
with [`StreamError::RecipientPayoutFailed`] if the token refuses the
payout (state rolls back unchanged).

functions.name: withdraw_many
functions.doc:
Claims the entire accrued balance of up to [`MAX_WITHDRAW_BATCH`] streams
in one transaction, through the exact single-stream claim path.

Every entry runs [`Self::settle_accrued`] — the same function
`withdraw_max` uses — so the batch inherits the CEI ordering, accrual
math, TTL extension and per-stream [`Withdrawn`] event of the audited
single path instead of restating any of it. One authorization covers the
batch: the caller must be the recipient of *every* stream listed, so a
holder can never claim a counterparty's stream by adding its id
(rejected per-entry with [`StreamError::NotAuthorized`]).

**Per-entry isolation.** A stream that fails a pre-payout check — not
found, not yours, not active, nothing accrued, overflow — comes back as a
[`WithdrawEntry`] carrying that error's code and `amount: 0`, and is
*skipped*: its siblings still pay out. Payout failures are the deliberate
exception:
[`StreamError::RecipientPayoutFailed`] aborts the whole call, because
the effects of a claim (the `withdrawn` update, the `Withdrawn` event)
are written *before* the token interaction, as CEI requires, and a
published event cannot be un-published. Skipping a failed payout would
therefore mean un-writing state after an external call — the exact
reentrancy hazard the ordering exists to prevent. Aborting instead lets
the host roll the transaction back as if it never ran.

**`strict`.** `false` (the default behaviour) keeps partial success: the
call settles what it can and reports the rest. `true` turns any
per-entry rejection into a revert of the whole call, returning that
error, so an all-or-nothing claim either settles every stream or none.

The call reverts before reading any state when `stream_ids` is empty
([`StreamError::WithdrawBatchEmpty`]), longer than
[`MAX_WITHDRAW_BATCH`] ([`StreamError::WithdrawBatchTooLarge`]), or
contains a repeated id ([`StreamError::WithdrawDuplicateStreamIds`]) —
a duplicate would otherwise claim against state its first occurrence has
already rewritten.

functions.name: cancel_stream
functions.doc:
Cancels a stream: pays the recipient their accrued-but-unwithdrawn
balance and refunds the sender the unaccrued remainder, atomically.

Callable by the sender always, and by the recipient only if the stream
was created with `cancelable = true`. Cancelling an already-cancelled
or depleted stream reverts with [`StreamError::StreamNotActive`].

Each payout leg maps a token-side failure to its own code —
[`StreamError::RecipientPayoutFailed`] for the recipient's accrued
share and [`StreamError::SenderRefundFailed`] for the sender's refund —
and any failure rolls the whole cancellation back: the stream stays
`Active`, `withdrawn` is restored, and no event survives.

# Ordering against `withdraw` (same-ledger race)

The counterpart of the ordering documented on
[`StreamingPayments::withdraw`]: cancellation is atomic and sees the
`withdrawn` balance as of *its* execution point.

* If the recipient's `withdraw` executes first, the cancel splits the
  remainder only (`streamed − withdrawn` to the recipient,
  `deposit − streamed` to the sender). If that withdrawal already
  drained the stream to `Depleted`, the cancel reverts with
  [`StreamError::StreamNotActive`] (code 5).
* If this cancel executes first, the stream is `Cancelled` and any
  later `withdraw` / `withdraw_max` reverts with
  [`StreamError::StreamNotActive`] (code 5).

Last write wins in execution order; no interleaving exists within a
ledger, and the losing call leaves state and balances untouched.
Pinned by the `race_*` regression tests in `test.rs`; see
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §6.1 for the race table.

functions.name: pause_stream
functions.doc:
Pauses an active stream (sender only), freezing accrual at the stream's
current clock. The recipient can still withdraw what accrued before the
pause; nothing further accrues until [`Self::resume_stream`]. Pausing an
already-paused stream returns [`StreamError::InvalidPauseTransition`].

functions.name: resume_stream
functions.doc:
Resumes a paused stream (sender only). The stream window (and any rate
segments) shift forward by the paused length, so accrual continues from
the frozen amount at the original rate and the full deposit still
streams. Resuming a stream that is not paused returns
[`StreamError::InvalidPauseTransition`].

functions.name: top_up
functions.doc:
Adds funds to an existing active stream. The deposit grows and accrual
remains linear over the original window, so the recipient's accrued
amount increases pro-rata immediately (Sablier-v1 `increaseAmount`
semantics).

Top-ups are rejected on cancelled or depleted streams. Topping up a
stream that has already passed `end_time` adds fully-accrued funds the
recipient can withdraw immediately.

A token-side failure to pull the funds returns
[`StreamError::TopUpTransferFailed`] and leaves `deposit` unchanged.

Note: extending `end_time` is intentionally not supported in v1 —
retroactively re-baselining accrual is lossy for the recipient; see
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for the design considerations and roadmap.

functions.name: raise_dispute
functions.doc:
Recipient-initiated dispute: flags this stream (wrong address,
coerced creation) and freezes its cancel/top-up mutations until the
sender calls [`StreamingPayments::resolve_dispute`] or the timelock
elapses and anyone calls [`StreamingPayments::expire_dispute`].

Only the stream's recipient can raise it (their authorization is
required), only on an active, undisputed stream. Anti-griefing: the
recipient posts a bond ([`StreamingPayments::required_dispute_bond`],
a share of the deposit that escalates with every dispute round on
the stream) via a prior token approval, held by the contract until
resolution. Accrual keeps running and accrued funds stay withdrawable
throughout — the freeze targets the stream's lifecycle, not the
recipient's earned balance.

Returns the recorded dispute (bond, window, expiry timestamp).

functions.name: resolve_dispute
functions.doc:
Sender-only resolution of an open dispute:

* `accept = true` — the dispute is legitimate: the bond is refunded
  to the recipient and the stream is unwound with the standard
  pro-rata cancel split (a `StreamCancelled` event accompanies the
  `DisputeResolved`). If the stream already depleted during the
  dispute (the recipient withdrew everything), only the bond is
  refunded.
* `accept = false` — bad faith: the bond is slashed to the sender as
  compensation for the frozen window, and the stream resumes normal
  operation immediately.

functions.name: expire_dispute
functions.doc:
Closes a dispute whose timelock has fully elapsed: the bond is split
(sender receives the upper half as compensation for the frozen
window, the recipient the remainder) and the stream resumes normally.

Callable by anyone once `now >= expires_at` — no authorization is
involved and no funds ever move to the trigger. Reverting the split
to a full bond refund would make serial disputes free for a patient
griefer; see `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for the griefing-threshold math.

functions.name: propose_ownership_transfer
functions.doc:
Proposes handing the caller's stream role (sender or recipient) to
`new_owner`. The role does not move until `new_owner` calls
[`StreamingPayments::accept_ownership_transfer`].

* Only the current sender or recipient may propose; their authorization
  is required. A stranger is rejected with [`StreamError::NotAuthorized`].
* The stream must be `Active`: ownership of a cancelled or depleted
  stream has no future claims and cannot be transferred.
* Proposing to the current holder of the same role is rejected with
  [`StreamError::InvalidTransferTarget`].
* At most one unexpired proposal exists per stream. Proposing again
  while one is pending reverts with
  [`StreamError::OwnershipProposalPending`]; an expired proposal is
  removed and replaced.

No tokens move and no accounting field changes at proposal time. The
target is recorded under its own storage key with a seven-day
acceptance window ([`OWNERSHIP_PROPOSAL_TTL_SECONDS`]).

functions.name: accept_ownership_transfer
functions.doc:
Accepts a pending ownership proposal. Only the proposal's `new_owner`
may call this, and their authorization is required.

On success the sender or recipient role moves to the caller. The
stream's accounting fields (`deposit`, `withdrawn`, `start_time`,
`end_time`, `token`, `status`, `use_oracle`) are untouched, so accrual
and the `0 <= withdrawn <= streamed <= deposit` invariant are unchanged:
what moves is the right to future payouts (recipient) or future top-ups
/ cancellation refunds (sender). The stream id is appended to the new
holder's discovery index; the previous holder's append-only index keeps
its historical entry.

Expired proposals cannot be accepted: the call reverts with
[`StreamError::OwnershipProposalExpired`]. Reverts roll back storage
writes, so the stale entry stays stored but is ignored forever after
its window; a later proposal replaces it (see
[`StreamingPayments::propose_ownership_transfer`]).

functions.name: cancel_ownership_transfer
functions.doc:
Cancels a pending ownership proposal. Only the current role holder that
created the proposal may cancel it; their authorization is required.

Cancelling is allowed after the proposal's acceptance window has
elapsed (it simply clears the stale entry). It emits no event: the
proposal never changed the stream, and `OwnershipProposed` remains the
permanent record that a proposal once existed.

functions.name: pending_ownership_transfer
functions.doc:
Read-only view of a stream's pending ownership proposal, if any.
Reading extends the proposal's storage TTL; unknown streams simply
return `None`.

functions.name: propose_sender_transfer
functions.doc:
Proposes handing the **sender** role of a stream to a new address.

Only the current sender may propose, and the proposal does not move the
role: a sender transfer changes who pays the recipient and who can
cancel the stream, so it is the *recipient's* decision to take. The
proposal therefore waits for [`StreamingPayments::accept_sender_transfer`]
from the recipient, inside `OWNERSHIP_PROPOSAL_TTL_SECONDS`.

`nonce` is the caller's freshness marker. It is stored with the proposal,
echoed by the proposal's events and must be repeated exactly by the
consent, so a consent can never land on a proposal that was replaced in
the meantime.

`transfer_refund_rights` decides, up front, what the recipient is
consenting to: with `false` (the default meaning auditors expect) the
deposit's refund claim stays with the original sender, and only the role
moves; with `true` the claim moves to `new_sender` as well. Refund rights
are never implied by a role change — the flag is the whole mechanism.

functions.name: accept_sender_transfer
functions.doc:
Executes a proposed sender transfer on the recipient's consent.

The caller must be the stream's **recipient** — the party whose
counterparty changes — and must present the proposal's nonce. On success
the role moves, the sender discovery indexes are re-pointed for both
sides, and the hop is appended to the stream's immutable sender log.
`deposit`, `withdrawn`, the time window and the token are untouched, so
accrual and the `0 <= withdrawn <= streamed <= deposit` invariant are
unchanged.

An elapsed window is [`StreamError::SenderTransferExpired`], never a
silent no-op; the stale entry is then reclaimed with
[`StreamingPayments::expire_sender_transfer`].

functions.name: expire_sender_transfer
functions.doc:
Reclaims a sender-transfer proposal whose acceptance window has elapsed.

Permissionless like the version-migration path: nothing about removing a
dead proposal can move funds or change an accounting field, so any keeper
may pay the gas to free the storage. Returns the reclaimed nonce so the
caller can confirm which proposal they removed.

Refuses while the proposal is still live ([`StreamError::
SenderTransferNotExpired`]) — the window, not a third party, is what ends
a recipient's option to consent — and with [`StreamError::
SenderTransferNotFound`] when there is nothing to reclaim.

functions.name: pending_sender_transfer
functions.doc: Read-only view of a stream's pending sender transfer, if any.

functions.name: sender_history
functions.doc:
The append-only sender-role log of a stream: who held the payer role at
creation and every consented hop since. Never rewritten, so the answer to
"who funded this deposit?" survives any number of transfers.

functions.name: refund_target
functions.doc:
The address that receives the refund of the unstreamed remainder when the
stream is cancelled. Equal to the current sender unless a sender transfer
left the claim behind (or an amendment moved it on purpose).

functions.name: propose_rate_change
functions.doc:
Proposes a new streaming rate for `stream_id`. The change takes
effect only when the counterparty calls
[`StreamingPayments::accept_rate_change`], and only from that moment
onward: everything accrued before it is untouched.

* Either party may propose; their authorization is required. A
  stranger is rejected with [`StreamError::NotAuthorized`].
* The stream must be `Active` and its window must not have elapsed:
  a rate for a finished stream would be a no-op that still rebalances
  funds, so it is rejected with [`StreamError::InvalidTimeRange`].
* `amount_per_second` must be positive ([`StreamError::ZeroAmount`]).
* At most one unexpired proposal exists per stream. Proposing again
  while one is pending reverts with
  [`StreamError::RateProposalPending`]; an expired proposal is
  removed and replaced.

Governance policy for the *proposed* rate is checked at acceptance,
not here: the ceilings that bind are the ones in force when the
change becomes effective, and they can move during the acceptance
window. No tokens move and no accounting field changes at proposal
time; the offer is recorded under its own storage key with a
seven-day acceptance window ([`RATE_PROPOSAL_TTL_SECONDS`]).

functions.name: accept_rate_change
functions.doc:
Accepts a pending rate change, rebalancing the deposit atomically.

Only the proposal's counterparty may accept, and their authorization
is required. The rate itself was fixed by the proposal; what acceptance
computes is what that rate now costs:

* `owed` — accrued at the change boundary `t` under the schedule that
  was in force until now, i.e. `streamed` at `t`. It is carried into
  the new schedule untouched, which is what makes the change unable to
  re-price the past.
* `reserved` — `amount_per_second * (end_time - t)`, an exact integer
  product, floored by nothing and rounded by nothing: the new segment
  accrues that amount over exactly that window, so it is fully streamed
  at `end_time` with no rounding residue.
* `adjustment` — `reserved - (deposit - owed)`. Positive means the
  old reserve no longer covers the new rate and the sender tops up the
  shortfall; negative means the sender is refunded the freed remainder.

The deposit becomes `owed + reserved`, so the accrual endpoint still
equals the deposit and the invariant `withdrawn <= streamed <= deposit`
holds across the whole change.

Funds movement follows the direction of the change: a top-up is pulled
*before* any effect is written (like `top_up`), so a token that refuses
the pull leaves the schedule and the deposit untouched; a refund is paid
*after* the effects (like `cancel_stream`), so a token that refuses the
refund rolls the whole acceptance back and the proposal survives for a
retry.

An expired proposal cannot be accepted
([`StreamError::RateProposalExpired`]), and neither can one whose parties
have moved on: if a role transferred after the offer was made, the
recorded proposer/counterparty pair is no longer the stream's sender and
recipient, and acceptance reverts with [`StreamError::NotAuthorized`].
The stale offer blocks nothing — its proposer can always cancel it.

functions.name: cancel_rate_change
functions.doc:
Cancels a pending rate proposal. Only the address that created it
may cancel, and its authorization is required.

Cancellation is allowed after the acceptance window elapsed (it simply
clears the stale entry) and on a stream that has since been cancelled
or depleted, which is what lets a proposer clean up after the fact.
It emits no event: the proposal never changed the stream, and
`RateChangeProposed` remains the permanent record that one existed.

functions.name: pending_rate_change
functions.doc:
Read-only view of a stream's pending rate proposal, if any.
Reading extends the proposal's storage TTL; unknown streams return
`None`.

functions.name: rate_segments
functions.doc:
Read-only view of a stream's rate schedule. Empty means the stream
still accrues at its original rate over `[start_time, end_time)`: the
single-window formula, with no stored segment to consult.

functions.name: get_stream
functions.doc: Read-only view of a stream's full state.

functions.name: get_dispute
functions.doc:
Read-only view of a stream's open dispute. Reverts with
[`StreamError::DisputeNotFound`] when the stream is undisputed
(disputes exist only while open; resolution and expiry remove them).

functions.name: required_dispute_bond
functions.doc:
The bond a recipient must post (and pre-approve) to raise the next
dispute on this stream: 5% of the deposit, multiplied by the number
of disputes already raised on it, floored at one token unit.

functions.name: available
functions.doc:
Read-only view of the accrued-but-unwithdrawn balance at the current
ledger time. Zero before `start_time` and for cancelled streams; the
full remainder at or after `end_time`.

functions.name: recipient_streams
functions.doc:
A page of stream ids where `recipient` is the recipient, in creation
order (oldest first). `limit` is clamped to `MAX_PAGE_SIZE`; paginate
by advancing `offset`. Unknown addresses yield an empty page.

Discovery view only: it does not authorize anything and terminal
(cancelled/depleted) streams keep their ids — read each stream's
`status` for lifecycle state.

functions.name: sender_streams
functions.doc:
A page of stream ids created by `sender`, in creation order. Same
pagination and advisory semantics as [`StreamingPayments::recipient_streams`].

functions.name: schedule_stream
functions.doc:
Pre-authorizes the creation of one or more streams at a future time and
escrows the up-front cost.

`sender` must authorize this call (their signature over the invocation
is verified by the host). The contract escrows
`(deposit_amount + fee_budget) * occurrences` of `token`:
`deposit_amount` per occurrence funds the stream, and `fee_budget` per
occurrence is the reward paid to whichever keeper later executes it.

* A **one-shot** intent is scheduled with `occurrences = 1` and
  `interval = 0`.
* A **recurring** intent is scheduled with `occurrences > 1` and a
  strictly positive `interval` (seconds between occurrence starts). The
  `i`-th occurrence's stream window is `[start_time + i*interval,
  end_time + i*interval)`.

Timing constraints: `execute_after <= start_time`, `now <= execute_after`
and `start_time` must be strictly in the future; `expires_at >
execute_after` bounds the execution window. The exact parameters are
committed into the intent's `params_hash`.

Returns the new intent id (monotonically increasing, starting at 1).

functions.name: execute_scheduled
functions.doc:
Executes the next due occurrence of a scheduled intent, creating the
stream and paying `keeper` the escrowed per-occurrence fee.

**Permissionless**: any address may call as `keeper`, but `keeper` must
authorize the call (so the fee cannot be front-run and redirected to a
copycat). The contract enforces that the intent is pending, is within its
`[execute_after, expires_at)` window for the next occurrence, and that
its stored parameters still match the scheduling commitment.

Execution is **once per occurrence**: each call decrements
`occurrences_remaining`, and a second call for an already-executed
occurrence (or a completed one-shot) reverts with
[`StreamError::IntentNotPending`]. Returns the created stream id.

functions.name: cancel_scheduled
functions.doc:
Cancels a pending scheduled intent and refunds the sender the escrow for
every outstanding occurrence.

Only the intent's sender may cancel (their authorization is required),
and only **before the execution window opens** (`now < execute_after`).
Once the window is open, keepers may execute and cancellation is
disallowed ([`StreamError::IntentNotCancellable`]) to remove a
cancel/execute race that would otherwise burn keeper gas. After
`expires_at`, use [`StreamingPayments::reclaim_expired`] instead.

functions.name: reclaim_expired
functions.doc:
Reclaims a pending intent that passed `expires_at` without being fully
executed, refunding the sender the escrow for every outstanding
occurrence.

**Permissionless**: anyone may trigger the refund (the funds always go
to the sender), so abandoned intents cannot lock capital indefinitely.
Reverts with [`StreamError::IntentExpired`]-style semantics via
[`StreamError::IntentNotExpired`] if called too early, and with
[`StreamError::IntentNotPending`] if the intent is terminal.

functions.name: get_intent
functions.doc: Read-only view of a scheduled intent's full state.

functions.name: sender_intents
functions.doc:
A page of scheduled-intent ids created by `sender`, in creation order.
Same pagination and advisory semantics as
[`StreamingPayments::sender_streams`].

functions.name: set_fee_bps
functions.doc:
Sets the protocol fee rate (basis points on each new stream's
deposit, charged once at creation). Governor-only. Reverts with
[`StreamError::FeeRateTooHigh`] above [`MAX_FEE_BPS`] (the protocol
cap) and with [`StreamError::NotGovernor`] for any other caller.

Changes apply only to streams created afterwards: fees are a
property of the deposit boundary a stream actually crossed, never
retroactively.

Once the governance signer set is bootstrapped this path closes and the
action must arrive as an executed proposal ([`StreamError::GovernanceTimelockRequired`]).

functions.name: nominate_governor
functions.doc:
Nominates `new_governor` as the next treasury governor (governor-only,
step 1 of a two-step rotation). Two steps mean a typo'd address can
never irreversibly strand the treasury: only an address that can
prove control (`accept_governor`) ever becomes governor.

functions.name: accept_governor
functions.doc:
Completes a governor rotation (step 2): the nominated address proves
control by authorizing this call and becomes the governor. Reverts
with [`StreamError::NoPendingGovernor`] when nothing is pending and
[`StreamError::NotGovernor`] for a caller who is not the nominee.

functions.name: withdraw_treasury
functions.doc:
Withdraws accumulated protocol fees for `token` to `recipient`.
Governor-only; bounded by fees collected minus fees already
withdrawn ([`StreamError::InsufficientTreasuryBalance`]).

Effects-interactions ordered: `FeeWithdrawn` is emitted and the
accounting persisted *before* the token transfer. A token-side failure
to pay out returns [`StreamError::TreasuryPayoutFailed`], rolling the
recorded withdrawal and the event back with it.

functions.name: treasury_status
functions.doc:
One-call treasury snapshot for `token`: governor, pending nominee,
current fee configuration, and the fee ledger totals that must
reconcile with the `FeeCharged` / `FeeWithdrawn` event streams.
Public, read-only, no auth.

functions.name: stream_fee
functions.doc:
The protocol fee charged for `stream_id` at creation, in smallest
token units. Zero for streams created while fees were disabled (or
whose fee rounded to zero). Reverts with
[`StreamError::StreamNotFound`] for unknown ids.

functions.name: verify_treasury
functions.doc:
One bounded page of the fee verification scan: sums stored
per-stream fees for `token` over a window of the stream-id space
(`count` clamped to [`MAX_PAGE_SIZE`]). Page from id 1 until `done`
is true; the summed `fees_in_range` values must equal
`treasury_status(token).charged_total` — and both must equal the
amounts in the contract's `FeeCharged` events. That three-way
equality is the treasury invariant, verifiable by anyone from
public reads alone (see `scripts/verify-fees.ts`).

functions.name: total_streams
functions.doc:
Number of streams ever created (ids are `1..=total_streams()`).
Public convenience for verifiers to know the scan range.

functions.name: register_sponsor
functions.doc:
Registers (or reconfigures) a sponsor budget and its authorized operator
(relayer) key. See [`sponsor`].

functions.name: set_sponsor_active
functions.doc: Pauses or resumes a sponsor's budget.

functions.name: rotate_operator_key
functions.doc: Rotates a sponsor's authorized operator (relayer) key.

functions.name: enroll_beneficiary
functions.doc: Binds (or rotates) a beneficiary's ed25519 consent key.

functions.name: sponsored_withdraw
functions.doc:
Relays a beneficiary's withdrawal with a sponsor absorbing the gas. See
[`sponsor`] for the inner-authorization and budget semantics.

functions.name: get_sponsor
functions.doc: Reads a sponsor's budget configuration, if any.

functions.name: get_beneficiary_public_key
functions.doc: Reads a beneficiary's enrolled consent key, if any.

functions.name: sponsor_period_spend
functions.doc: The sponsor's current-window spend.

functions.name: beneficiary_spend
functions.doc: A beneficiary's spend within a sponsor's current window.

functions.name: policy_init
functions.doc:
Initializes the policy module with `admin`. Callable once only; panics
if called again. Admin authorization is required.

functions.name: policy_propose_asset
functions.doc:
Queues an allowlist mutation (adding or removing `asset`) with a
timelock delay. Callable only by the current admin.

functions.name: policy_execute_asset
functions.doc:
Executes a queued asset allowlist change after the timelock has elapsed.

Callable by anyone: once a change has been vetted by the admin and the
public timelock delay has expired, execution is permissionless so it
cannot be stalled or held hostage by an absent admin.

functions.name: policy_propose_handoff
functions.doc: Proposes a new admin for the two-step handoff (admin-only).

functions.name: policy_accept_handoff
functions.doc:
Accepts the pending admin handoff. Callable only by the proposed new
admin, consuming their authorization and clearing the proposal.

functions.name: policy_cancel_handoff
functions.doc: Cancels a pending admin handoff (admin-only).

functions.name: policy_admin
functions.doc: Returns the current policy admin, if initialized.

functions.name: policy_pending_admin
functions.doc: Returns the pending policy admin nominee, if any.

functions.name: policy_timelock_delay
functions.doc: Returns the on-chain timelock delay in seconds.

functions.name: policy_set_timelock_delay
functions.doc: Sets the timelock delay in seconds (admin-only).

functions.name: policy_is_asset_allowed
functions.doc: Read-only check whether `asset` is currently allowed for new streams.

functions.name: policy_get_queued_asset
functions.doc: Returns the queued allowlist change for `asset`, if any.

functions.name: set_stream_policy
functions.doc:
Sets governance policy floors and ceilings for streams of `token`, or global default if `token` is None.
Governor-only.

Gated by the governance timelock once the signer set is bootstrapped: the
action then arrives as `GovernanceAction::SetStreamPolicy` on an executed
proposal (see `governance.rs`).

functions.name: get_stream_policy
functions.doc: Queries the effective stream policy for `token` (falling back to global policy if unset).

functions.name: schema_version
functions.doc: Returns the current schema version of stored contract state.

functions.name: is_frozen
functions.doc: Returns whether mutating contract operations are currently frozen.

functions.name: set_frozen
functions.doc:
Sets the freeze state of the contract. Governor-only.

When frozen, mutating stream entrypoints (create, withdraw, withdraw_max,
cancel, top_up) revert with [`StreamError::ContractFrozen`], but read views
remain accessible.

Freezing stays immediate even after governance is bootstrapped: a
timelock that delays the break-glass is worse than no break-glass.
*Unfreezing* reopens the contract to activity, so it requires an executed
proposal.

functions.name: propose_upgrade
functions.doc:
Proposes a Wasm bytecode upgrade with an enforced timelock delay. Governor-only.

`delay_seconds` must be at least [`MIN_UPGRADE_DELAY_SECONDS`] (24 hours).
Overwrites any existing proposal.

functions.name: cancel_upgrade
functions.doc:
Cancels a pending upgrade proposal. Governor-only.

Reverts with [`StreamError::NoPendingUpgrade`] if no proposal is pending.

Like freezing, this is a risk-reducing action and so stays immediate: a
maliciously proposed upgrade must be cancellable the second it is seen,
not two days later.

functions.name: execute_upgrade
functions.doc:
Executes a pending upgrade proposal once its timelock delay has elapsed. Governor-only.

Updates the contract executable via [`env.deployer().update_current_contract_wasm`]
and clears the pending upgrade.

functions.name: pending_upgrade
functions.doc: Read-only view of any pending upgrade proposal.

functions.name: migrate_storage
functions.doc:
Migrates a batch of streams from schema v1 to schema v2. Governor-only.

Requires the contract to be frozen ([`StreamError::ContractNotFrozen`]).
`count` is clamped to [`MAX_MIGRATION_BATCH_SIZE`] (50 streams per call).
If `start_id == 0`, migration resumes from `migration_cursor + 1`.
When the cursor reaches `total_streams`, the schema version is bumped to v2.
Calling this after migration is complete reverts with [`StreamError::AlreadyMigrated`].

functions.name: migration_progress
functions.doc: Read-only snapshot of storage migration progress.

functions.name: stream_record_version
functions.doc:
The storage layout version of a single stream record.

`1` is the legacy untagged layout (a bare `Stream` map), `2` the
version-tagged [`VersionedStream`] every current write produces. Auditors
use this to answer "what still needs moving?" per stream without
decoding the record itself; see `scripts/migrate_audit.ts` for the
off-chain walk.

Fails closed with [`StreamError::SchemaVersionUnsupported`] for a record
tagged with a layout this build does not understand, and with
[`StreamError::StreamNotFound`] when no record exists.

functions.name: migrate_stream_version
functions.doc:
Re-encodes one stream record under [`CURRENT_STREAM_RECORD_VERSION`].

**Idempotent: running it twice is a no-op.** A record that already
carries the current layout is reported with `migrated == false` and is
not rewritten, so it emits no event and changes no storage byte. Repeat
calls are safe from any number of keepers racing on the same stream.

**Permissionless**: unlike the governor-driven [`StreamingPayments::
migrate_storage`] batch, anyone may migrate a single record — it moves
no funds and touches no accounting field, only the encoding of a stream
whose decoded state is provably unchanged. It is also gas-bounded by
construction: exactly one stream record is read and (at most) one
rewritten per call, so callers never pay for somebody else's backlog.

Returns [`StreamError::StreamNotFound`] for an unknown id and
[`StreamError::SchemaVersionUnsupported`] for a record this build cannot
decode (there is nothing to re-encode *from*, so refusing is the only
safe answer). Migration is refused while the contract is frozen, like
every other state-mutating entrypoint.

functions.name: set_oracle_config
functions.doc:
Configures the oracle publisher set, threshold, and staleness bound.
Authorized by the treasury governor.

functions.name: submit_oracle_time
functions.doc: Records an authorized external time feed report.

functions.name: resolve_time
functions.doc: Resolves reference timestamp for a given stream id and oracle flag.

functions.name: oracle_config
functions.doc: Reads current oracle configuration.

functions.name: oracle_report
functions.doc: Reads latest report from a publisher.

functions.name: governance_bootstrap
functions.doc:
Establishes the governance signer set and its veto window. Governor-only,
and one-time: after bootstrap the set can only change by executing a
`GovernanceAction::SetSigners` proposal, so no key can ever re-establish
governance over an existing one.

Until this is called every admin entry point behaves exactly as it did
before the timelock existed, which makes adoption an explicit, auditable
act rather than a side effect of a wasm upgrade.

Reverts with [`StreamError::GovernanceDuplicateSigner`] when the set lists
the same address twice and [`StreamError::GovernanceSignersNotDistinct`]
when it holds fewer than two distinct keys — the invariant is two
*independent* signatures, not two slots.

functions.name: governance_propose
functions.doc:
Proposes an admin action for the timelock. Signer-only; returns the
proposal id.

functions.name: governance_sign
functions.doc:
Adds the caller's signature to a proposal. Reverts with
[`StreamError::GovernanceDuplicateSignature`] if they already signed.

functions.name: governance_veto
functions.doc:
Vetoes a proposal while its window is open. One signer is enough: vetoing
removes risk, so it should never be the action that requires a quorum.

functions.name: governance_execute
functions.doc:
Applies a matured, multiply-signed proposal.

Permissionless on purpose: a proposal that only a particular keyholder
can submit is one that keyholder can suppress. `executor` is recorded in
the audit trail but authorizes nothing — the authority is the two
signatures on the proposal.

functions.name: governance_is_initialized
functions.doc: Whether the timelock has taken over the admin entry points.

functions.name: governance_signers
functions.doc: The current signer set.

functions.name: governance_veto_window
functions.doc: The configured veto window in seconds.

functions.name: governance_proposal
functions.doc: Reads a proposal: its window, recorded signatures and terminal flags.

functions.name: governance_proposal_count
functions.doc: The next proposal id, for clients that want to follow the queue.

structs.name: StreamInput
structs.doc: Parameters for one stream in a [`StreamingPayments::create_streams`] call.

structs.name: Dispute
structs.doc:
An open dispute on a stream. Stored only while the dispute is live;
resolution/expiry deletes the entry.

fields.name: raised_by
fields.doc: The stream recipient who raised it (always the stream's recipient).

fields.name: bond
fields.doc: Bond held by the contract for the duration of the dispute.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: First ledger timestamp at which the dispute can be expired.

structs.name: Proposal
structs.doc: A proposed admin action awaiting its veto window and signatures.

fields.name: executable_at
fields.doc: First ledger timestamp at which the proposal may execute.

fields.name: signers
fields.doc: Distinct signatures recorded so far, in signing order.

structs.name: OracleConfig
structs.doc: Oracle configuration stored in instance storage.

fields.name: publishers
fields.doc: Authorized oracle publishers.

fields.name: threshold
fields.doc: Minimum number of fresh publisher reports required for quorum.

fields.name: max_stale_seconds
fields.doc: Maximum staleness in seconds before a report is considered stale.

structs.name: OracleReport
structs.doc: An individual report from an authorized publisher.

fields.name: reported_time
fields.doc: The external reference timestamp.

fields.name: ledger_time
fields.doc: Ledger timestamp when the report was recorded on-chain.

structs.name: ResolvedTime
structs.doc: Result of resolving reference time for a stream.

fields.name: timestamp
fields.doc: The resolved reference timestamp.

fields.name: is_oracle
fields.doc: Whether the timestamp came from oracle aggregation (`true`) or ledger fallback (`false`).

structs.name: StreamPolicy
structs.doc: Governance-managed policy floors and ceilings for streams.

structs.name: QueuedAssetChange
structs.doc: Queued policy change for an asset awaiting timelock expiry.

fields.name: allowed
fields.doc: Desired allowlist state (true = allowed, false = removed).

fields.name: queued_at
fields.doc: Timestamp when the change was queued.

fields.name: executable_after
fields.doc: Ledger timestamp at or after which the change can be executed.

structs.name: ScheduledIntent
structs.doc:
A sender-authorized, keeper-executable intent to create one or more streams.

`deposit` and `fee_budget` are *per occurrence*: the sender escrows
`(deposit + fee_budget) * occurrences_total` at scheduling time. Each
execution creates one stream and pays the keeper one `fee_budget`.

fields.name: deposit
fields.doc: Deposit escrowed for *each* occurrence.

fields.name: start_time
fields.doc: Scheduled start of the first occurrence.

fields.name: end_time
fields.doc: Scheduled end of the first occurrence (`end_time > start_time`).

fields.name: cancelable
fields.doc: Whether created streams may be cancelled by their recipient.

fields.name: interval
fields.doc: Seconds between occurrence starts; `0` for a one-shot intent.

fields.name: occurrences_total
fields.doc: Total occurrences this intent will ever create (`>= 1`).

fields.name: occurrences_remaining
fields.doc: Occurrences not yet materialized.

fields.name: fee_budget
fields.doc: Keeper fee escrowed for *each* occurrence (`>= 0`).

fields.name: execute_after
fields.doc: Earliest time the first occurrence may be executed.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: After this time no occurrence may be executed.

fields.name: params_hash
fields.doc: SHA-256 commitment over every immutable scheduling parameter.

structs.name: SponsorConfig
structs.doc:
A sponsor's budget policy. The sponsor address is the map key, so it is not
repeated here.

fields.name: token
fields.doc:
The single token this sponsor will fund claims against. A claim whose
stream uses any other token is rejected: caps are per-token, otherwise a
sponsor capping cheap tokens could be drained on expensive ones.

fields.name: per_period_limit
fields.doc: Maximum total payout the sponsor will absorb per `window_seconds`.

fields.name: per_beneficiary_limit
fields.doc: Maximum payout to a single beneficiary per `window_seconds`.

fields.name: window_seconds
fields.doc:
Budget period length in seconds. Spend counters reset when the ledger
timestamp crosses `period_start + window_seconds`.

fields.name: active
fields.doc:
When false, all claims against this sponsor are rejected. Lets a sponsor
stop the bleeding without deleting (or losing) its budget state.

structs.name: PeriodSpend
structs.doc:
Spend accumulated within one budget window. Reused for both the
sponsor-global and the per-beneficiary counters.

fields.name: period_start
fields.doc: Ledger timestamp at which the current window began.

fields.name: spend
fields.doc: Total payout absorbed in the current window.

structs.name: PendingOwnership
structs.doc:
A pending two-step ownership proposal for one stream.

Proposals live under their own storage key ([`DataKey::PendingOwnership`])
rather than inside [`Stream`], so accepting or cancelling one leaves the
stream's accounting fields untouched and the dedicated key can be given its
own TTL treatment.

fields.name: proposed_by
fields.doc:
The current role holder that created the proposal (and the only address
allowed to cancel it).

fields.name: new_owner
fields.doc: The address that must accept the role before it takes effect.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: Ledger timestamp at or after which the proposal is stale.

structs.name: PendingSenderTransfer
structs.doc:
Lifecycle state of a stream.
A pending sender-role transfer that the *recipient* must consent to.

[`PendingOwnership`] moves a role with only the incoming holder's
acceptance; a sender change is different in kind, because the recipient's
counterparty — who they get paid by, and who can cancel the stream — is
being swapped under them. So the transfer is proposed by the current
sender and only executes on the recipient's consent
(`accept_sender_transfer`), inside the proposal's window.

`nonce` is the caller's freshness marker: it is stored with the proposal,
echoed by every event in its lifecycle, and must be repeated exactly by the
consenting call. A proposal that was replaced (and so carries a different
nonce) cannot be executed by accident.

fields.name: sender_from
fields.doc:
The sender at the time the proposal was made, and the address whose
authorization is required to propose it.

fields.name: new_sender
fields.doc: The address that will hold the sender role once the recipient consents.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: Ledger timestamp at or after which the proposal is stale.

fields.name: transfer_refund_rights
fields.doc:
Whether consenting also moves the refund claim for the existing deposit
(see [`SenderTransferRecord::refund_rights_transferred`]). Fixed at
proposal time so the recipient consents to exactly one meaning.

structs.name: SenderTransferRecord
structs.doc: One executed sender transfer, appended to [`SenderHistory::transfers`].

fields.name: at
fields.doc: Ledger timestamp at which the recipient's consent executed the transfer.

fields.name: refund_rights_transferred
fields.doc:
True when the amendment explicitly moved the refund claim for the
existing deposit to `sender_to`. False means the deposit keeps accruing
to the original sender's claim even though the role moved — refund
rights are only ever moved on purpose, never implied by a role change.

structs.name: SenderHistory
structs.doc:
Append-only ledger of who held the sender role for one stream.

`sender_at_creation` is the first entry of the record kept for a stream, and
the log is never rewritten: consenting to a transfer appends exactly one
[`SenderTransferRecord`]. That is what lets an auditor answer "who funded
this deposit?" after several hops, which the mutable `Stream::sender` field
alone cannot.

structs.name: RateSegment
structs.doc:
One window of a stream's piecewise rate schedule.

A segment reserves `allocation` tokens for the half-open window
`[start_time, end_time)` and accrues them pro rata over `basis_seconds`:

```text
floor(allocation * elapsed_within_window / basis_seconds)
```

`basis_seconds` is normally the window's own length, which makes the term
exact (no rounding at all) whenever `allocation` is a whole multiple of it —
the shape every renegotiated segment has, because it is priced as
`amount_per_second * window_length`. It is the *original* stream duration for
the first segment of a renegotiated stream, whose `allocation` is the deposit
the schedule started from: keeping that pair untouched is what makes an
accepted change unable to re-price the past.

Because each window is a sub-interval of the stream, the elapsed part of it
is never longer than `basis_seconds`, which is the condition
[`validate_capacity`] needs to guarantee the product cannot overflow.

fields.name: start_time
fields.doc: First timestamp this segment accrues at (inclusive).

fields.name: end_time
fields.doc: Last timestamp this segment accrues at (exclusive).

fields.name: allocation
fields.doc: Tokens reserved for the window, as of the segment being accepted.

fields.name: basis_seconds
fields.doc: Divisor of the pro-rata term; see the struct docs.

structs.name: PendingRateChange
structs.doc:
A pending two-step rate change for one stream.

Like [`PendingOwnership`], this lives under its own storage key
([`DataKey::PendingRateChange`]) rather than inside [`Stream`], and the
schedule it would install lives under [`DataKey::RateSegments`]. Neither is
part of the `Stream` entry, so an existing stream's stored XDR keeps its
layout: a stream created before this feature accrues exactly as it did, and a
rate change that is proposed and then cancelled leaves no trace in the
stream's accounting fields.

fields.name: proposed_by
fields.doc:
The stream party that created the proposal (and the only address allowed
to cancel it).

fields.name: counterparty
fields.doc: The other party: the address whose acceptance makes the change effective.

fields.name: amount_per_second
fields.doc:
The proposed rate, in whole token units per second, for the window that
starts when the proposal is accepted.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc:
Ledger timestamp at or after which the proposal is stale. What the
proposal commits to is the *rate*; the funds movement it implies is
computed from the schedule at the moment it is accepted.

structs.name: Stream
structs.doc:
Full state of a payment stream.

Field order and names are the storage wire format: appending a field is a
schema change that bumps [`CURRENT_STREAM_RECORD_VERSION`], and the field
must be an `Option` (or defaulted by a migration) so older records keep
decoding.

fields.name: deposit
fields.doc: Total amount funded into the stream (original deposit + top-ups).

fields.name: withdrawn
fields.doc: Total amount paid to the recipient so far (withdrawals + cancel payout).

fields.name: cancelable
fields.doc: If true, the recipient may also cancel and reclaim their accrued balance.

fields.name: use_oracle
fields.doc:
If true, settles against external oracle time feed instead of ledger time.
Optional because records written before the oracle clock existed carry no
`use_oracle` key at all; the SDK decodes an absent field as `None`, which
means ledger time. Every stream this build writes sets `Some(_)`, so the
on-ledger shape of new records is unchanged.

structs.name: StreamVersionReport
structs.doc:
Outcome of [`migrate_stream_record`]: which layout a single stream moved
from and to, and whether it moved at all.

fields.name: migrated
fields.doc:
False when the record already carried the current layout, so nothing was
rewritten — the proof that migration is idempotent.

structs.name: BatchEntry
structs.doc: Parameters for creating a single stream within a batch creation call.

structs.name: WithdrawOutcome
structs.doc:
Proposed contract upgrade pending timelock expiration.
One settled entry of a `withdraw_many` batch claim.

`withdraw_many` answers every requested id (see [`WithdrawEntry`]) and this
type describes money that actually moved, so it is also what the batch's
[`crate::BatchWithdrawSummary`] event lists.

fields.name: amount
fields.doc:
The whole accrued-but-unwithdrawn balance delivered for this stream.
Always positive: an entry that had nothing to pay is an `Err`, not a
zero-amount outcome.

structs.name: WithdrawEntry
structs.doc:
The per-entry answer of [`crate::StreamingPayments::withdraw_many`], one per
requested id and in request order.

This is deliberately a struct carrying an amount *or* a code, rather than a
`Vec<Result<WithdrawOutcome, StreamError>>`. Soroban encodes `Result::Err` as
an `ScError`, and the off-chain ScVal decoder (`scValToNative` in
`@stellar/stellar-sdk`) has no conversion for it, so a batch with even one
skipped entry would arrive as a decode failure instead of a partial result —
defeating the point of per-entry isolation. A map per entry always decodes,
and `code` is the same stable discriminant the contract reports on a revert.

fields.name: amount
fields.doc: Tokens delivered for this stream; `0` when the entry was skipped.

fields.name: code
fields.doc:
`0` once the entry settled, otherwise the [`crate::StreamError`] that
skipped it, as its numeric code.

structs.name: PendingUpgrade
structs.doc: Proposed contract upgrade pending timelock expiration.

structs.name: MigrationStatus
structs.doc: Progress report for on-chain storage migration.

structs.name: TreasuryStatus
structs.doc:
One call snapshot of the treasury state for a token: governance, current
fee configuration, and the fee ledger totals that verifiers reconcile
against events and per-stream fees.

fields.name: token
fields.doc: The token this accounting belongs to.

fields.name: governor
fields.doc: Current treasury governor.

fields.name: pending_governor
fields.doc: Pending governor nominee, if a rotation is awaiting acceptance.

fields.name: fee_bps
fields.doc: Currently configured fee rate in basis points (0 = fees disabled).

fields.name: max_fee_bps
fields.doc: The protocol cap on `fee_bps` (published so clients need no constant).

fields.name: charged_total
fields.doc: Total fees ever charged for this token (Σ `FeeCharged` events).

fields.name: withdrawn_total
fields.doc: Total fees ever withdrawn for this token (Σ `FeeWithdrawn` events).

fields.name: collectible
fields.doc: Fees currently held: `charged_total - withdrawn_total`.

structs.name: FeeScan
structs.doc:
Result of one bounded verification scan over the stream-id space
(see [`crate::StreamingPayments::verify_treasury`]).

fields.name: token
fields.doc: Token whose fees were scanned.

fields.name: start_id
fields.doc: First stream id of the scan window.

fields.name: scanned_count
fields.doc:
Number of stream ids actually examined (window may be shorter than
requested near the end of the id space).

fields.name: fees_in_range
fields.doc: Sum of per-stream stored fees within the window.

fields.name: next_start
fields.doc:
Where the next scan window starts (scan is finished when
`done` is true).

fields.name: done
fields.doc:
True when the window reached the end of the id space — paging from
id 1 until `done` visits every stream exactly once.

enums.name: IntentStatus
enums.doc: Lifecycle state of a scheduled intent.

cases.name: Pending
cases.doc: Authorized and (partially) executable; some occurrences remain.

cases.name: Executed
cases.doc: Every occurrence has been materialized into a stream. Terminal.

cases.name: Cancelled
cases.doc: Cancelled by the sender before the execution window opened. Terminal.

cases.name: Expired
cases.doc:
Passed `expires_at` with occurrences outstanding; escrow refunded.
Terminal.

enums.name: OwnershipRole
enums.doc: The role being handed over by a two-step ownership transfer.

cases.name: Sender
cases.doc: The payer: may top up and cancel, and receives cancellation refunds.

cases.name: Recipient
cases.doc: The claimant: may withdraw accrued funds.

cases.name: Active
cases.doc: Running; funds accrue and can be withdrawn or topped up.

cases.name: Cancelled
cases.doc: Cancelled; remaining funds were split at cancellation. Terminal.

cases.name: Depleted
cases.doc: Fully streamed and fully withdrawn. Terminal.

unions.name: GovernanceAction
unions.doc:
One admin action that may be proposed, timelocked and executed.

The payloads mirror the direct entry points exactly, so dispatch is a
one-to-one call into the same internal helper rather than a second
implementation of the same authority.

cases.name: SetFeeBps
cases.doc: `set_fee_bps`

cases.name: SetStreamPolicy
cases.doc: `set_stream_policy`

cases.name: SetFrozen
cases.doc: `set_frozen` — unfreezing goes through the timelock; freezing does not.

cases.name: WithdrawTreasury
cases.doc: `withdraw_treasury(token, recipient, amount)`

cases.name: NominateGovernor
cases.doc: `nominate_governor` — step one of the two-step rotation.

cases.name: ProposeUpgrade
cases.doc: `propose_upgrade(new_wasm_hash, delay_seconds)`

cases.name: ExecuteUpgrade
cases.doc: `execute_upgrade`

cases.name: MigrateStorage
cases.doc: `migrate_storage(start_id, count)`

cases.name: SetOracleConfig
cases.doc: `set_oracle_config(publishers, threshold, max_stale_seconds)`

cases.name: SetSigners
cases.doc: Replace the signer set. A rotation of the keys that govern this contract.

cases.name: SetVetoWindow
cases.doc: Replace the veto window.

events.name: StreamCreated
events.doc: Emitted when a new stream is created and its deposit pulled in.

events.name: StreamsCreated
events.doc: Emitted once after an atomic batch creates its streams.

events.name: Withdrawn
events.doc: Emitted when the recipient withdraws accrued funds.

dataFields.name: withdrawn_total
dataFields.doc: Total withdrawn from the stream after this withdrawal.

events.name: BatchWithdrawSummary
events.doc:
Emitted once after a `withdraw_many` batch settles, alongside the
per-stream [`Withdrawn`] events. The per-stream shape is unchanged so
existing consumers keep working; this event is the batch-level view: every
entry that paid, the total, and how many of the requested ids were skipped.

dataFields.name: settled
dataFields.doc:
Entries that settled, in request order. A skipped entry appears only in
the entrypoint's return value, never here — nothing was paid for it.

dataFields.name: total
dataFields.doc: Sum of the delivered amounts: the total the recipient received.

dataFields.name: requested
dataFields.doc: Ids the caller asked for.

dataFields.name: skipped
dataFields.doc: `requested - settled.len()`: entries skipped with a per-entry error.

events.name: StreamCancelled
events.doc:
Emitted when a stream is cancelled. The recipient's accrued balance and
the sender's refund are both paid atomically in the same transaction.

dataFields.name: recipient_amount
dataFields.doc: Amount paid out to the recipient at cancellation.

dataFields.name: sender_amount
dataFields.doc: Amount refunded to the sender at cancellation.

events.name: StreamToppedUp
events.doc: Emitted when the sender adds funds to an existing stream.

dataFields.name: new_deposit
dataFields.doc: Stream deposit after the top-up.

events.name: StreamPaused
events.doc: Emitted when the sender pauses a stream, freezing accrual at `paused_at`.

dataFields.name: paused_at
dataFields.doc: Stream-clock timestamp at which accrual was frozen.

events.name: StreamResumed
events.doc:
Emitted when the sender resumes a paused stream. The window shifts by
the paused length, so accrual continues from the frozen point.

dataFields.name: new_end_time
dataFields.doc: The stream's `end_time` after shifting it by the paused length.

events.name: StreamScheduled
events.doc:
Emitted when a sender pre-authorizes a future (optionally recurring)
stream creation and escrows the deposit plus keeper fee budget.

dataFields.name: deposit
dataFields.doc: Deposit escrowed for *each* occurrence.

dataFields.name: start_time
dataFields.doc:
Scheduled start of the first occurrence (later occurrences are shifted
by `interval`).

dataFields.name: end_time
dataFields.doc: Scheduled end of the first occurrence.

dataFields.name: interval
dataFields.doc: Seconds between occurrence starts; `0` for a one-shot intent.

dataFields.name: occurrences
dataFields.doc: Total number of streams this intent will create.

dataFields.name: fee_budget
dataFields.doc: Keeper fee escrowed for *each* occurrence.

dataFields.name: execute_after
dataFields.doc: Earliest time the first occurrence may be executed.

dataFields.name: expires_at
dataFields.doc: After this time no occurrence may be executed; the escrow is reclaimable.

events.name: ScheduledStreamExecuted
events.doc:
Emitted when a keeper executes one occurrence of a scheduled intent,
creating the stream and paying itself the escrowed per-occurrence fee.

dataFields.name: stream_id
dataFields.doc: The newly created stream id.

dataFields.name: occurrence_index
dataFields.doc: Zero-based index of the occurrence just executed.

dataFields.name: occurrences_remaining
dataFields.doc: Occurrences still outstanding after this execution.

dataFields.name: fee_paid
dataFields.doc: Fee paid to the keeper for this execution.

events.name: ScheduledIntentCancelled
events.doc:
Emitted when a sender cancels a not-yet-executable intent and is refunded
the escrow for all outstanding occurrences.

dataFields.name: refund
dataFields.doc: Total refunded (deposit + fee budget for every outstanding occurrence).

events.name: ScheduledIntentExpired
events.doc:
Emitted when an intent passed `expires_at` with occurrences outstanding and
its escrow was returned to the sender.

dataFields.name: refund
dataFields.doc: Total refunded for the outstanding occurrences.

events.name: FeeCharged
events.doc:
Emitted exactly once per funded stream that owes a protocol fee, in the
same transaction as (and immediately after) `StreamCreated`. Keyed by
`stream_id` so fee history is auditable per stream; the stream's stored
fee (`stream_fee` read) and the token's `treasury_status` totals must
always reconcile with the sum of these events — that reconciliation is
the treasury invariant, checkable by anyone via `verify_treasury` and
`scripts/verify-fees.ts`.

dataFields.name: payer
dataFields.doc: The sender who paid the fee on top of the deposit.

dataFields.name: amount
dataFields.doc: Fee amount in smallest token units (deposit * fee_bps / 10_000, floored).

dataFields.name: fee_bps
dataFields.doc: The fee rate in basis points that produced this amount.

events.name: FeeWithdrawn
events.doc:
Emitted when the treasury governor withdraws accumulated protocol fees for
one token. Keyed by `token` (treasury accounting is per token);
`withdrawn_total` carries the cumulative withdrawn amount so event
consumers can reconcile against `treasury_status` without reading state.

dataFields.name: governor
dataFields.doc: The governor who authorized the withdrawal.

dataFields.name: recipient
dataFields.doc: Where the withdrawn fees were sent.

dataFields.name: withdrawn_total
dataFields.doc: Total fees withdrawn for this token after this withdrawal.

events.name: DisputeRaised
events.doc:
Emitted when the recipient raises a dispute, freezing the stream's
cancel/top-up mutations until resolution or expiry. The bond (stream
token, held by the contract) accompanies the flag.

dataFields.name: bond
dataFields.doc: Bond pulled into the contract for the duration of the dispute.

dataFields.name: expires_at
dataFields.doc: First ledger timestamp at which the dispute can be expired.

events.name: DisputeResolved
events.doc:
Emitted when the sender resolves an open dispute. `accept = true`
refunds the bond to the recipient and unwinds the stream pro-rata
(a `StreamCancelled` event accompanies it); `accept = false` treats the
dispute as bad-faith and slashes the bond to the sender, resuming the
stream normally.

dataFields.name: accept
dataFields.doc: Whether the sender accepted the dispute as legitimate.

dataFields.name: bond
dataFields.doc:
The bond at stake (paid to the recipient on accept, slashed to the
sender otherwise).

events.name: DisputeExpired
events.doc:
Emitted when a dispute's timelock expires without a verdict: the stream
resumes and the bond is split, `sender_share` rounding up.

dataFields.name: sender_share
dataFields.doc:
Half of the bond (rounded up) paid to the sender as compensation for
the frozen window.

dataFields.name: recipient_share
dataFields.doc: The remainder of the bond refunded to the recipient.

events.name: SponsorRegistered
events.doc:
Emitted when a sponsor registers (or reconfigures) a gas-sponsorship
budget. Keyed by the sponsor address; the `registered` symbol lets indexers
separate budget setup from sponsored claims.

events.name: SponsorActiveSet
events.doc: Emitted when a sponsor pauses or resumes its budget.

events.name: BeneficiaryEnrolled
events.doc:
Emitted when a beneficiary binds an ed25519 consent key, and again whenever
they rotate it. Keyed by the beneficiary address.

events.name: OperatorKeyRotated
events.doc:
Emitted when a sponsor rotates its authorized operator (relayer) key. The
previous operator key stops validating relay signatures immediately.

events.name: SponsorClaim
events.doc:
Emitted when a claim is sponsored and paid out: the operator relayed the
beneficiary's withdrawal and the sponsor's budget absorbed the gas. The
payout still flows from the stream, exactly as in an unsponsored withdraw.

events.name: PolicyInitialized
events.doc: Emitted when the policy module is initialized with its initial admin.

events.name: PolicyAssetQueued
events.doc: Emitted when an asset allowlist mutation is proposed and queued under timelock.

events.name: PolicyAssetExecuted
events.doc: Emitted when a queued asset allowlist change is executed after timelock expiry.

events.name: PolicyHandoffProposed
events.doc: Emitted when the admin proposes a new admin in step 1 of the two-step handoff.

events.name: PolicyHandoffAccepted
events.doc: Emitted when the proposed admin accepts the handoff in step 2.

events.name: PolicyHandoffCancelled
events.doc: Emitted when a pending admin handoff is cancelled by the current admin.

events.name: UpgradeProposed
events.doc: Emitted when a contract upgrade is proposed with a timelock delay.

events.name: UpgradeCancelled
events.doc: Emitted when a pending contract upgrade is cancelled by the governor.

events.name: ContractUpgraded
events.doc: Emitted when a contract upgrade is executed after its timelock has elapsed.

events.name: ContractFrozenStateChanged
events.doc: Emitted when the contract freeze state is toggled by the governor.

events.name: StorageMigrated
events.doc: Emitted when a batch of streams is migrated to a new storage schema version.

events.name: StreamRecordMigrated
events.doc:
Emitted when a single stream's storage record is re-encoded under a new
layout version. Only fired when a rewrite actually happened: an
already-current record migrates as a silent no-op, so the absence of this
event is what makes repeated `migrate_stream_version` calls idempotent.

events.name: StreamPolicySet
events.doc: Emitted when a stream policy floor/ceiling configuration is updated.

events.name: OracleConfigUpdated
events.doc: Emitted when the oracle configuration is updated by governance.

events.name: OracleTimeReported
events.doc: Emitted when an authorized oracle publisher reports a reference timestamp.

events.name: OracleStaleFallback
events.doc:
Emitted when oracle time resolution falls back to native ledger time due to
stale feed, insufficient reports, or unconfigured registry.

events.name: OwnershipProposed
events.doc:
Emitted when a current sender or recipient proposes handing their role to a
new address. The handoff takes effect only when the target accepts.

dataFields.name: current_owner
dataFields.doc: The current role holder (must be the stream's sender or recipient).

dataFields.name: new_owner
dataFields.doc: Address that must accept before the role moves.

dataFields.name: expires_at
dataFields.doc: Ledger timestamp at or after which the proposal is stale.

events.name: OwnershipAccepted
events.doc:
Emitted when a proposed ownership handoff is accepted by its target. The
stream's accounting fields (`deposit`, `withdrawn`, time window) are
unchanged; only the role address moves.

dataFields.name: previous_owner
dataFields.doc: The role holder before the transfer.

dataFields.name: new_owner
dataFields.doc: The new role holder (the accepting address).

events.name: RateChangeProposed
events.doc:
Emitted when the sender or recipient proposes a new streaming rate. The
change takes effect only when the counterparty accepts, and only from the
moment of acceptance: nothing accrues differently before it, and the
`RateChangeAccepted` event that follows carries the settled amounts.

dataFields.name: proposed_by
dataFields.doc: The proposing party (the stream's sender or recipient).

dataFields.name: counterparty
dataFields.doc: The party whose acceptance the change requires.

dataFields.name: expires_at
dataFields.doc: Ledger timestamp at or after which the proposal is stale.

events.name: RateChangeAccepted
events.doc:
Emitted when a pending rate change is accepted and its rebalancing settles.

The four amounts are the whole funds-bug audit trail for one change, and
they are exact by construction: `reserved_at_new_rate` is an integer product
(`new_amount_per_second * window length`) and `deposit` is
`owed_at_change + reserved_at_new_rate`. `adjustment` is the signed
difference against the deposit before the change — positive means the sender
topped up that amount, negative means the sender was refunded its absolute
value, zero means the old reserve still covered the new rate exactly.

dataFields.name: accepted_by
dataFields.doc: The accepting counterparty (the address that authorized the change).

dataFields.name: new_amount_per_second
dataFields.doc:
Rate in effect from `effective_from` (inclusive) to the stream's
`end_time`; the rate the proposal committed to.

dataFields.name: effective_from
dataFields.doc: First timestamp accrued at the new rate.

dataFields.name: owed_at_change
dataFields.doc:
Accrued at `effective_from` under the previous schedule. The change
cannot alter this amount — that is the property the segment split keeps.

dataFields.name: reserved_at_new_rate
dataFields.doc: Reserved for `[effective_from, end_time)` at the new rate.

dataFields.name: adjustment
dataFields.doc: Funds moved to settle the change (see the struct docs).

dataFields.name: deposit
dataFields.doc:
Stream deposit after the adjustment; equals
`owed_at_change + reserved_at_new_rate`.

events.name: GovernanceSignersSet
events.doc:
Emitted when the signer set is established or rotated, and when the veto
window changes. The set is emitted in full because "which keys govern this
contract" is only auditable from the transcript, not from a delta.

events.name: GovernanceActionProposed
events.doc:
Emitted when a signer proposes an admin action. `executable_at` is the end of
the veto window: from that timestamp the proposal is executable by anyone and
is never voided by time.

events.name: GovernanceActionSigned
events.doc:
Emitted for each distinct signature. A second signature from an address that
already signed is refused before this event can fire, so `signature_count`
here is always a count of distinct keys.

events.name: GovernanceActionVetoed
events.doc: Emitted when a signer vetoes a proposal inside its veto window.

events.name: GovernanceActionExecuted
events.doc:
Emitted when a matured, multiply-signed proposal is applied. `executed_by` is
whoever submitted the transaction — execution is permissionless — while
`signers` names the keys that actually authorized it.

events.name: SenderTransferProposed
events.doc:
Emitted when the sender proposes handing the payer role to a new address.
Unlike [`OwnershipProposed`], this handoff is not completed by the target's
acceptance: the *recipient* consents, because changing who pays them (and
who can cancel on them) is their risk to take.

dataFields.name: nonce
dataFields.doc: The proposal's freshness marker, which the consenting call must repeat.

dataFields.name: transfer_refund_rights
dataFields.doc: Whether consenting also moves the refund claim for the existing deposit.

events.name: SenderTransferred
events.doc:
Emitted when the recipient's consent executes a proposed sender transfer.
`sender_from` / `sender_to` name both sides of the hop; the accounting
fields of the stream are untouched.

dataFields.name: refund_rights_transferred
dataFields.doc:
False when the deposit's refund claim stayed with the original sender —
the default, and the reason this is a field rather than an inference.

events.name: SenderTransferExpired
events.doc:
Emitted when a proposal that aged out of its acceptance window is reclaimed,
freeing its storage. The role never moved.

events.name: StreamRefundTargetChanged
events.doc:
Emitted whenever the refund claim of a stream is pinned to a new address —
at creation (`create_stream_with_refund`) or later by the sender
(`set_refund_target`). The unstreamed remainder of the deposit is paid to
`new_target` on cancellation instead of to the sender. Accrual, the
recipient's claims and who may cancel are untouched: this is a destination
change, not a value change.

dataFields.name: previous_target
dataFields.doc:
The address that held the claim before this change: the previous
`new_target`, or the sender on the first routing of a stream.

dataFields.name: at_creation
dataFields.doc:
True when the routing was set by `create_stream_with_refund`, so a
reader can tell a creation-time destination from a later amendment.
